businessModel: Free browser bundled with Avast security software; PRO subscription adds a browser VPN and stronger blocking. New-tab page carries sponsored shortcuts and affiliate placements, and search/shopping partners are listed in the product policy.
paidNote: PRO about $39.99 first year for five devices, $49.99 renewal (antivirus-review.com, checked Jul 2026)
updateCadence: Auto-updates; no public build-to-Chromium map. The 152 build was listed in late Sep 2026 while Chrome 156 reached stable on 2026-10-20.
summary: A proprietary Chromium browser from Gen Digital with Bank Mode, ad and tracker blocking, anti-fingerprinting and a paid VPN. Its own policy says it is not telemetry-free, and Avast's Jumpshot history weighs on trust.
bestFor: Avast antivirus users who want Bank Mode (it needs the browser)
People who want blocking and phishing protection without installing extensions
Chrome users who want a familiar Chromium interface with extra safeguards
notFor: Anyone who wants a telemetry-free or independently audited browser
People who object to sponsored new-tab shortcuts or a bundled-installer model
Windows 7/8 users (no new installs; stuck on v109)

pros.title: Bank Mode
pros.detail: Opens banking and shopping sites in an isolated virtual desktop that blocks screen capture, but it needs Avast Antivirus installed.

pros.title: Strong phishing results
pros.detail: Scored 94% (Jan 2026) and 89% (Mar 2026) in AV-Comparatives phishing tests with no false alarms, ahead of Chrome (72%, 77%) and Firefox (75%, 76%).

pros.title: Privacy Guard
pros.detail: Combines ad blocking, tracker filtering and anti-fingerprinting in Basic, Balanced and Strict modes.

pros.title: Chromium compatibility
pros.detail: Same engine as Chrome, so sites work as they do in Chrome.

pros.title: Extra guards
pros.detail: Extension Guard, Webcam Guard, Hack Check, Screen Sharing Mode and end-to-end encrypted sync (per Avast).

cons.title: Not telemetry-free
cons.detail: Avast's policy lists server-side URL subsets (kept 36 months), usage events, device data and third-party analytics such as Google Analytics and Mixpanel.

cons.title: Jumpshot legacy
cons.detail: The FTC finalised a $16.5 million order in June 2024 over Avast selling re-identifiable browsing data through Jumpshot (2014-2020).

cons.title: Hidden bundled extensions
cons.detail: Researcher Wladimir Palant found 11 Avast extensions, some hidden and some weakening security, and advised running it only in a VM.

cons.title: Monetised and slow to track Chrome
cons.detail: Sponsored new-tab shortcuts and Bing as default search; the 152 build trails Chrome 156 by weeks.

faq.q: Is Avast Secure Browser the same as AVG Secure Browser?
faq.a: Effectively yes: both are the same Chromium-based browser marketed under two brands owned by Gen Digital.
Yes. Avast's own product policy says it is not a telemetry-free browser, listing URL subsets, usage events, device and extension data, plus third-party analytics.

faq.q: Can I use Chrome Web Store extensions?
faq.a: Sources conflict: one review says it only offers Avast's curated add-on page, another describes Chrome-style extension compatibility. Check the extensions page in the app.
